newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-FORMER UNION BOSS JAILED FOR FRAUD.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FORMER UNION BOSS JAILED FOR FRAUD.

text.p: The former executive director of Australia's New South Wales Rugby Union was jailed on Friday for five years after being convicted of fraud involving payments of supposedly amateur players.

Ken Elphick, 45, was found guilty last November of 25 fraud charges amounting to Australian $601,000 ($457,000) in relation to the multi-million dollar redevelopment of the Concord Oval rugby ground in Sydney's western suburbs during the 1980s.
The New South Wales state District Court had been told during the trial the fraud involved funds from two NSWRU subsidiary companies involved in the redevelopment of Concord Oval.
Elphick claimed during his trial he had the authority to use a "slush fund" to deal with certain "commercially sensitive" matters, which included payment to rugby union players to promote the game.
He said more than 40 famous but unnamed players had received payments of between A$500 and A$3,000 to play and promote the game during the late 1980s.
Elphick told the court he was "honour bound" not to mention the details of certain cheques because they were confidential and that their disclosure could damage the sport.

The rules of rugby union at the time strictly prohibited the payment of players to take part in the then amateur game. Claims of "shamateurism" however dogged the sport, with player payments acknowledged as widespread in the game's strongholds of Australia, New Zealand, South Africa and Europe.
The prosecution argued during the case Elphick had carried out the fraud by use of "an artful device" and that he had had almost total control of large sums of money.
District Court judge Thomas Davidson sentenced Elphick to a maximum of five years in jail and set a non-parole period of two-and-a-half years.

Rugby union became fully professional in 1996 after a $550 million international broadcasting rights deal was signed the previous year between media magnate Rupert Murdoch's international conglomerate News Corp Ltd and the unions of Australia, New Zealand and South Africa.
Concord Oval is rarely used, with major matches in Sydney played exclusively at the inner-city Sydney Football Stadium.
